title: Simple programs capture how genetic programs generate biological forms

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Simple programs capture how genetic programs generate biological forms

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Simple programs can reproduce many features of biological organisms and appear to capture essential mechanisms by which genetic programs generate observed biological forms, enabling new models and general abstract theories in biology.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 1: The Foundations for a New Kind of Science

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: such programs can reproduce many features of biological organisms—and for example seem to capture some of the essential mechanisms through which genetic programs manage to generate the actual biological forms we see.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 1, “The Foundations for a New Kind of Science”; section “Relations to Other Areas” (from p. 7), p. 9. Scope: biological morphogenesis and pigmentation patterns

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch01-11: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public developmental imaging permits tests in particular systems. The claims about many organismal features and essential genetic mechanisms require broad causal data that are not currently unified or adequately covered.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit explicit simple-program developmental models to public imaging and genetic perturbation data for selected organisms. Test whether they predict held-out morphology and perturbation responses better than rival developmental models at comparable complexity.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Matched genotype, dynamics, and morphology data are limited across organisms.

Visual resemblance alone does not identify an essential mechanism.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public morphology and model-organism genetics can test whether particular simple programs reproduce particular forms and whether the known genes do something similar. That is a handful of systems, not morphogenesis in general. Mechanistic rivals remain compatible with the same images, so the data support case studies and do not confirm that simple programs capture the essential genetic mechanisms.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare explicit program models with measured morphologies and with identified genetic regulatory mechanisms, on a pre-registered set of patterns such as pigmentation and branching. Confirmation requires a mechanistic match, not only a similar picture. A rival developmental model that fits the same images and the genetic interventions refutes the claim for that case.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Reaction-diffusion and positional-information models fit many of the same forms.

Imaging and genetic coverage is concentrated on a few model organisms.

Pattern similarity does not show that the genetic program works as the model does.
